title: Cross-Embodiment Causal Transfer from Human Videos to Robot Manipulation
abstract: arXiv:2610.21798v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Scaling robot manipulation models requires large amounts of interaction data, yet collecting diverse real-robot experience remains costly. Human manipulation videos, in contrast, provide abundant and diverse task experience that could potentially benefit robot learning. However, differences in morphology, action spaces, and control mechanisms make human motions unsuitable as direct supervision for robot actions, raising a scientific question: what knowledge in human videos should be transferred across embodiments to robot manipulation? To address this question, we analyze subtask transfer through the lens of causal beams, focusing on which contextual conditions and interaction dependencies should be retained to support local task effects. Based on this perspective, we propose Causal-Beam-Guided Subtask Transfer (CBST). translated_title: 跨具身因果迁移：从人类视频到机器人操作
translated_abstract: 扩展机器人操作模型需要大量的交互数据，然而收集多样化的真实机器人经验仍然成本高昂。相比之下，人类操作视频提供了丰富且多样的任务经验，有望促进机器人学习。然而，由于形态结构、动作空间和控制机制上的差异，人类动作并不适合直接作为机器人动作的监督信号，由此引出一个科学问题：人类视频中的哪些知识应当跨具身迁移到机器人操作中？为了回答这一问题，我们通过“因果束”（causal beams）的视角分析子任务迁移，聚焦于应当保留哪些上下文条件和交互依赖以支持局部任务效果。基于这一视角，我们提出了因果束引导的子任务迁移方法。CBST 从人类视频中学习与操作相关的表示，并将其落实到任务级语义变量中。
tldr: 提出因果束引导的子任务迁移方法（CBST），通过因果束视角识别人类视频中应跨具身迁移的上下文条件与交互依赖，从而将人类视频中的知识有效迁移到机器人操作学习中。
en_tdlr: Proposes Causal-Beam-Guided Subtask Transfer (CBST), which uses a causal beam perspective to identify which contextual conditions and interaction dependencies from human videos should be transferred across embodiments to improve robot manipulation learning.
